full_judgment:
2. The decree-holder Rupali Bank obtained Mortgage decree on 2-5-85 in Mortgage Suit No. 21 of 1985 in the court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Commercial Court, Chittagong against the judgment-debtor Messer Sunrise Tea House. In pursuance of the aforesaid decree Mortgage Execution Case No.5 of 1992 was started and the mortgaged property, was sold in auction and it was auction-purchased by the respondent. Subsequently, the sale was confirmed. In such circumstances, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Assistant Custodian Vested Property, Chittagong, namely, the petitioner filed an application in the executing court under Order 21 rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The said application was rejected upto the Appellate Division. Thereafter, the executing court passed an order staying money Execution Case No.5 of 1992 till disposal of Other Suit No. 68 of 1992. Again, the auction purchaser- respondent filed an application for reconsideration of the order but the same was also rejected. 

 3. Respondent Nos. 3-17 as plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 68 of 1992 impleading auction- purchaser and others including the petitioner as defendants for a declaration that the judgment and decree obtained in the Mortgage Suit No. 21 of 1985 is illegal, void and fraudulent.In that suit, they prayed for stay of the Execution Case No.5 of 1995 arising out of the Mortgage suit. In that suit the trial Court by an order dated 11-3-95 stayed the Execution Case and also stayed the issuance of the sale certificate in favour of the auction-purchaser- respondent. 

 6. The learned Judges of the High Court Division correctly held that auction sale having taken place and the sale having been confirmed the issuance of sale certificate in favour of the auction- purchaser cannot be illegally withheld by parties not connected with the mortgage suit or with the mortgage execution case. The learned Judges also found that the application under Order 21 rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable as the decree under Mortgage Execution Case No.5 of 1992 is not a decree against the present petitioner. Hence, the learned Judges of the High Court Division correctly held that the order of stay granted till disposal of Other Suit No. 68 of 1992 is illegal and not called for in the facts of the present case.
